countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

Programmes in this category cover process design, thermodynamics, mass and heat transfer, reaction engineering and plant operations. Each university's own award title, entry rules and fees are shown on its programme page.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering
courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree covering structural analysis and design, geotechnical engineering, transportation engineering, water resources, environmental engineering, surveying and construction management. Programmes pair lecture teaching with materials, hydraulics and surveying laboratories, site visits and a final-year design project. Graduates work in construction, infrastructure, consultancy and public works, or continue to a master's specialisation.

Teaching is built around workshop practice, thermal and materials laboratories, computer-aided design and a final-year project. Graduates move into manufacturing, automotive, energy, thermal and design roles, or continue to a master's specialisation such as thermal engineering or machine design.

universities.name: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani
universities.summary: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani (BITS Pilani) is a private deemed-to-be university headquartered in Pilani, Rajasthan, and a Government of India Institution of Eminence. Foreign-passport holders join through its SAT-based International Students Admission scheme, which offers English-taught B.E. and integrated M.Sc. degrees at the Pilani, K K Birla Goa and Hyderabad campuses.
universities.campusLifestyle: BITS Pilani reports more than 16,500 students on its three Indian campuses, all fully residential. Pilani houses about 4,500 students in 11 boys' hostels and a girls' hostel complex, with a 65,000 sq ft library of about 2,30,000 volumes, a 25 m pool and a Student Activities Centre. The K K Birla Goa campus covers 180 acres above the Zuari River, and the Hyderabad campus over 200 acres. Students run clubs and festivals, including BOSM (sports), OASIS (culture) and APOGEE (academics) at Pilani.
universities.cityProfile: Pilani is a town of about 50,000 people in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan, about 200 km west of Delhi and 220 km north of Jaipur. Temperatures range from about 45 C in summer to 0 C in winter, with about 30 cm of rain a year. The K K Birla Goa campus at Zuarinagar is 4.5 km from Goa airport, 10 km from Vasco da Gama, 22 km from Margao and about 25 km from Panaji; Goa is warm and humid, and July is the wettest month. The Hyderabad campus at Jawaharnagar, Shameerpet (Medchal district, Telangana) is about 27 km from Hyderabad city and 70 km from Rajiv Gandhi International Airport; summer highs often pass 40 C between April and June. Banking is on or next to each campus: an ICICI ATM at Pilani with an SBI branch in the adjoining CEERI campus, an SBI branch and HDFC ATM at Goa, and an SBI branch in the Hyderabad campus shopping complex.
universities.practicalExposure: Every integrated first degree ends with Practice School or a thesis. Practice School I is an eight-week placement with an organisation in the summer after the second year. Practice School II places final-year students with an organisation for about five and a half months under faculty supervision; students who choose the thesis instead spend the same period on a research topic at BITS or a collaborating organisation. Degrees are credit-based, need at least 144 units and normally take eight semesters, though students may finish faster or slower. M.Sc. students can compete after the first year, on their BITS grades, for a second B.E. degree under the dual-degree scheme. The Pilani campus adjoins CSIR's Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute, a national laboratory.
universities.hostelOverview: All three campuses are fully residential, with separate hostels for men and women. For the 2026-27 ISA intake, hostel and internet charges are INR 82,250 per semester, plus a mess and electricity advance of INR 10,000 and other advances of INR 12,000 per semester; the advance is adjusted against actual bills each semester, and food and electricity beyond it are charged separately. A summer term costs 50 per cent of the semester hostel fee. Goa and Hyderabad rooms are furnished, with internet, round-the-clock security and floor common rooms. Parents can book the VFAST guest house at Pilani.
universities.dietarySupport: At Pilani, each pair of boys' hostels shares a kitchen-cum-mess and the girls' hostel has its own mess; every mess serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and is run by a students' committee. Mess bills are settled against the INR 10,000 per-semester advance. Pilani also has the AKSHAY supermarket of the BITS consumers' cooperative, and Goa and Hyderabad each have an on-campus shopping complex.
universities.safetyOverview: Hostels at the Goa and Hyderabad campuses have round-the-clock security. The Pilani Medical Centre has a full-time physician and a gynaecologist in morning and evening outpatient hours, a weekly dental surgeon and paediatrician, and a clinical laboratory; Goa and Hyderabad also have campus medical centres. Health insurance is not part of the ISA fee.
universities.studentSupport: The Office of International Students facilitates FRRO/FRO registration, due within 14 days of arrival. A paid orientation week covers local travel, room and board and a guided city tour. ISA queries go to each campus: bitsisa@pilani.bits-pilani.ac.in (Pilani), isagoa@goa.bits-pilani.ac.in (Goa) and admissions@hyderabad.bits-pilani.ac.in (Hyderabad).

faq.question: Is BITS Pilani public or private?
faq.answer: BITS Pilani is a private deemed-to-be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956; its deemed status dates from a notification of 18 June 1964, and it appears on UGC's list of deemed universities. UGC also lists it as an Institution of Eminence in the private category, notified on 14 October 2020.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: BITS Pilani states that all lectures and official communications are in English, with no switch to another language later in the degree. The ISA scheme asks for adequate proficiency in English at Grade 12 but publishes no separate IELTS or TOEFL minimum.

faq.question: Who can apply through the ISA scheme?
faq.answer: Only citizens of countries other than India who hold a foreign passport. Indian citizens apply through BITSAT instead. A foreign national may apply through both ISA and BITSAT if they meet each route's rules, but the two routes run on different timelines and fee tiers.

faq.question: What school results do I need?
faq.answer: Grade 12 (10+2) or equivalent with Physics and Mathematics plus one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology or a technical vocational subject, with at least 75 per cent aggregate in the three and 60 per cent in each. B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering also accepts Biology in place of Mathematics. CAIE students need these subjects at A Level and IB students at Higher Level. In the 2026 cycle, Grade 12 had to be taken in 2026 or passed in 2025.

faq.question: Which SAT score does BITS Pilani need?
faq.answer: The minimum is 1160 out of 1600 on the SAT (Reading and Writing plus Mathematics), and the 2026 cycle accepted tests taken on or after 1 February 2024. SAT Subject Tests are not needed, and superscores may be entered. Send scores through College Board to DI code 7759. Merit is ranked on the SAT score, with ties broken by years of schooling outside India and then the SAT Mathematics score; BITS may also interview applicants.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Apply online through the ISA page at admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ISA/ISA.html, upload Grade 12 marksheets, photographs and a passport valid for at least six months from joining, and pay the INR 7,000 application fee. Offers are released in iterations in SAT merit order. Accepting an offer means paying the first-semester fee, after which BITS issues the admission letter for the visa. Students Traffic can help you plan SAT timing and programme and campus preferences.

faq.question: When is the intake and when should I apply?
faq.answer: There is one intake a year, with the first semester starting in August. In the 2026 cycle the application window ran from December 2025 to 8 April 2026, SAT scores had to reach BITS by 15 April, and a second window from 3 to 22 June covered vacant seats only. Dates for the 2027 intake had not been published by September 2026.

faq.question: How much does the first year cost in total?
faq.answer: For a non-SAARC student admitted in 2026-27, the ISA fee sheet adds up to INR 19,08,890 for year one before the merit waiver: INR 14,85,000 tuition, INR 1,64,500 hostel and internet, INR 44,000 in mess and other advances, INR 4,160 union fee, and one-time charges of INR 2,11,230 including the application fee and a refundable INR 32,000 deposit. Food and electricity beyond the advance, health insurance and visa fees are extra. SAARC tuition is INR 4,37,250 per semester.

faq.question: Are scholarships available?
faq.answer: Every ISA admit receives a merit tuition waiver in the first semester: 80 per cent for the top 4 per cent, 50 per cent for the next 10 per cent, 30 per cent for the next 20 per cent and 15 per cent for the rest. Later waivers are awarded semester by semester and need a CGPA of at least 8.0 for the 80 per cent tier or 6.0 for the others, within the normal programme duration only.

faq.question: Is BITS Pilani recognised and accredited?
faq.answer: UGC lists BITS Pilani as a deemed-to-be university and an Institution of Eminence. NAAC accredited it A++ with a CGPA of 3.68 in its fourth cycle, declared on 29 November 2024, and NIRF 2025 ranks it 7th among universities, 11th in Engineering and 2nd in Pharmacy. How the degree is recognised in your home country depends on your national authorities, so check with them before enrolling.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply after admission?
faq.answer: Apply for an Indian student visa at the Indian embassy or consulate in your country using the BITS admission letter, and make sure it is endorsed to BITS Pilani; BITS advises allowing at least three weeks. A change of institution later needs a new visa from home. Register with the FRRO/FRO within 14 days of arrival; the Office of International Students helps. Work is not permitted on a student visa.

faq.question: What does accommodation cost?
faq.answer: All three campuses are fully residential with separate hostels for men and women. For the 2026-27 ISA intake, hostel and internet charges are INR 82,250 per semester, plus an INR 10,000 mess and electricity advance and INR 12,000 in other advances each semester. Mess food is billed against the advance, and a summer term costs half the semester hostel fee.

faq.question: Should I apply through ISA or BITSAT?
faq.answer: ISA is built for foreign-passport holders: admission is ranked on the SAT, not BITSAT, and it covers the 11 B.E. branches and six integrated M.Sc. degrees on the Pilani, Goa and Hyderabad campuses. BITSAT also leads to other routes, such as the 2+2 international programmes, but runs on a different timetable. Students Traffic can help you compare both routes against your SAT and Grade 12 profile.

SAARC nationals, billed on the lower SAARC rupee tuition tier
restrictions: Only citizens of countries other than India (foreign passport holders) can use the ISA scheme; Indian citizens apply through BITSAT

admissionsContent.overview: The M.Sc. (Integrated First Degree) Semiconductor and Nanoscience is a four-year degree entered straight after Grade 12, with no intermediate bachelor's degree, taught in English at BITS Pilani's Hyderabad Campus (Jawaharnagar, Shameerpet, Telangana). Foreign-passport holders are admitted through the SAT-based ISA scheme. Through ISA it is also offered at Pilani and K K Birla Goa.

eligibility.intro: Entry is through the ISA scheme for foreign-passport holders, on Grade 12 results with Physics and Mathematics and a SAT score; merit is ranked on the SAT.
items: Citizenship of a country other than India, shown by a foreign passport valid for at least six months from the joining date
Grade 12 (10+2) or equivalent with Physics and Mathematics compulsory plus one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology or a technical vocational subject, and adequate proficiency in English
At least 75 per cent aggregate in Physics, Mathematics and the third subject, with at least 60 per cent in each; CAIE applicants need these at A Level and IB applicants at Higher Level
SAT total of at least 1160 out of 1600 (Reading and Writing plus Mathematics); the 2026 cycle accepted tests taken on or after 1 February 2024
Grade 12 taken for the first time in the admission year or passed in the year before (2026 cycle: 2026 or 2025); only the latest attempt counts
Applicants without Chemistry at Grade 12 must complete a Chemistry bridge course in the first semester

applicationSteps: Take the SAT (Reading and Writing plus Mathematics) and have College Board send the score to BITS Pilani with DI code 7759; SAT superscores may be entered on the form
Complete the ISA online application linked from admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ISA/ISA.html within the application window and pay the INR 7,000 application fee online
Upload Grade 12 marksheets (or submit them in the later Grade 12 window if results are pending), photographs and a copy of the passport
Follow the admission iterations on the ISA website: offers are made in SAT merit order and campus preference, and BITS may call applicants for an interview
Accept the offer by paying the first-semester fee by the stated deadline; BITS then issues the admission letter used for the student visa
Obtain an Indian student visa endorsed to BITS Pilani, report to the allotted campus for orientation and register with the FRRO/FRO within 14 days of arrival

academic: Grade 12 (10+2) marksheet and certificate, or A Level / IB Higher Level results
Official SAT score report sent by College Board to DI code 7759
Grade 10 marksheet and certificate
application: Passport copy, valid for at least six months from the joining date
Recent photographs
ISA online application acknowledgement and INR 7,000 fee receipt
BITS Pilani admission letter, issued after the first-semester fee is paid
Indian student visa endorsed to BITS Pilani

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: The 2026 ISA window ran from December 2025 to 8 April 2026, SAT scores were due by 15 April and a 3-22 June window covered vacant seats only. Classes began in August 2026. Dates for the 2027 intake were not yet published in September 2026.
visaConsiderations: The student visa must be endorsed to BITS Pilani; changing institution later needs a fresh visa applied for from the home country
Register with the FRRO/FRO within 14 days of arrival (PIO/OCI cardholders excepted); the Office of International Students helps with this
Employment is not permitted on an Indian student visa

programmes.mediumNote: BITS Pilani states that all lectures and official communications are in English.
programmes.feeNotes: BITS Pilani's ISA fee structure for students admitted in 2026-27 sets non-SAARC tuition at INR 7,42,500 per semester (INR 14,85,000 in year one), rising to INR 7,79,500, 8,18,500 and 8,59,500 per semester in the following years, INR 64,00,000 over eight semesters. SAARC nationals pay INR 4,37,250 per semester in year one (INR 37,68,500 over four years). Every admitted student gets a merit tuition waiver of 15 to 80 per cent. Also payable: one-time admission fee INR 1,56,100, orientation facilitation fee INR 16,130 and refundable caution deposit INR 32,000; per semester, hostel and internet INR 82,250, mess and electricity advance INR 10,000 and other advances INR 12,000; INR 4,160 a year to the Students' Union and Student Aid Fund. At the ECB reference rate of 21 September 2026 (USD 1 = INR 95.82), year-one non-SAARC tuition is about USD 15,500. Fees for the 2027-28 intake are not yet published.

teachingPhases.phase: Four-year integrated first degree, eight semesters
teachingPhases.details: Delivered at the Hyderabad Campus, Jawaharnagar, Shameerpet, Telangana. The final year includes either Practice School II (about five and a half months with an organisation) or a thesis; Practice School I is an eight-week summer placement after year two. An interdisciplinary degree in semiconductor materials, nanostructures, nanotechnology and materials science, listed under the Chemistry department.

teachingPhases.phase: Optional dual degree
teachingPhases.details: M.Sc. students can compete after the first year, on their BITS grades, for a second B.E. degree; the dual-degree route usually takes five years.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.

evidence.internalNotes: The brochure gives 12 December 2025 as the window opening; the later timeline PDF gives 1 December 2025. Public copy says 'December 2025'. BITSAT-2026 brochure gives 10 August 2026 as the first-semester start.

evidence.claimText: ISA fee structure 2026-27 (INR): non-SAARC tuition 7,42,500 per semester (AY 2026-27), 7,79,500 (2027-28), 8,18,500 (2028-29), 8,59,500 (2029-30); SAARC 4,37,250, 4,59,000, 4,82,000, 5,06,000; admission fee 1,56,100; facilitation fee 16,130; caution deposit 32,000; hostel and internet 82,250 per semester; mess advance 10,000; other advances 12,000; Students' Union 4,160; merit waivers 15-80%.
evidence.sourceLabel: BITS Pilani - Fee Structure for International Students Admission (ISA) Scheme 2026-27
evidence.internalNotes: The fee sheet is scheme-wide and applies to all ISA undergraduate programmes. evidence.claimText: BITS Pilani's programme page lists campus(es) 'Pilani, K K Birla Goa, Hyderabad' and a four-year integrated first degree; the BITSAT-2026 brochure's campus-wise programme list and the ISA brochure footnotes agree on campus availability.
evidence.sourceLabel: BITS Pilani - Integrated First Degree programme page (M.Sc. (Integrated First Degree) Semiconductor and Nanoscience)
evidence.internalNotes: M.Sc. programme pages show '05 Years' for some titles; the ISA brochure states M.Sc. programmes are four-year integrated degrees and the M.Sc. Biological Sciences page explains the five-year figure as the optional dual-degree route. Duration recorded as 4.

evidence.claimText: The ISA brochure FAQ states that all lectures and official communications at BITS are in English, and requires adequate proficiency in English at Grade 12; no IELTS or TOEFL minimum is published for ISA.

evidence.claimText: ISA brochure 2026-27: only citizens of a country other than India (foreign passport holders) may apply; Grade 12 with Physics and Mathematics compulsory plus one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Biology/technical vocational subjects, minimum 75% aggregate and 60% in each for B.E. and M.Sc.; SAT (new format) minimum 1160/1600, taken not earlier than 1 February 2024; Grade 12 in 2026 or passed in 2025; CAIE at A Level, IB at HL.
